findings.finding: W1 builds nine units in parallel, but U1 (the tag gate) changes the contract every other unit's PR must satisfy. Units U3–U10 each add tests. If U1 merges while its siblings are still in flight, every already-open W1 PR goes red at F11 for its own untagged tests — and the campaign's stop condition ("red twice → released") would then release units for a failure that is purely a sequencing artifact, not a code defect.
findings.suggestion: Either merge U1 alone first (a one-unit W0) before starting the rest of W1, or add a campaign-level pre-instruction so every W1 unit tags its own new tests from the start. The plan already recognizes authoring is "load-bearing" for U1; the same contract applies to the other nine PRs.  2. Category: dependency — Severity: medium

findings.finding: U3, U4, U5, and U6 all introduce fail-closed record requirements (reason codes at trivial, cascade completion, `surface=none` justification, FR naming on bugs) but their touch sets list only verifier/script files — no authoring-document updates (SKILL.md, F5c guidance, sub-iterate instructions). The agent writing the F5c entry won't know the new required fields exist until the verifier rejects it reactively. For autonomous units with a two-red budget, that guarantees wasted attempts.
findings.suggestion: Apply U1's pattern uniformly: any unit that changes what must be recorded must update the authoring instructions in the same diff. Add the relevant doc files to U3–U6's touch sets.  3. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: U1's exemption path is a self-reported closed-vocab code with no cross-check against the diff (unlike U6, which does diff-check its `change_type` exemptions). `fixture-or-helper` becomes a magic word that exempts anything. Worse, the §6 success criterion ("100% tagged, excluding exemptions") is trivially satisfiable by exempting everything — the campaign can pass its own verification while the whitepaper claim stays unenforced.
findings.suggestion: Report the exemption count (per reason code) in the §6 retrospective alongside the tagged share, and surface exemptions in the F12 summary so a reviewer can see how much of the gate is being bypassed.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: U6's diff-allowlist for `change_type` exemptions (`docs/`, tests, `.shipwright/`, `.github/`) contradicts its own vocabulary. A "tooling" exemption touching `scripts/`, `shared/scripts/`, `pyproject.toml`, or config files will be refused even though those are exactly tooling paths. This will block legitimate PRs and train agents to pick a different (wrong) code.
findings.suggestion: Align the allowlist with the closed-vocab codes — either add tooling-appropriate paths (`scripts/`, build/config files) or rename the codes to match what the allowlist actually permits.  5. Category: approach — Severity: medium

findings.finding: U9 switches the 80% hook from plan-section coverage to FR-bound-test coverage without measuring what the new number will be. With 6% of monorepo tests tagged today and U2 backfilling only the delta since 2026-09-16, FR/AC coverage by bound tests is plausibly far below 80% — the soft-block will fire on nearly every run, and constant logged overrides will normalize ignoring it, eroding the gate the change is meant to strengthen.
findings.suggestion: Before switching the metric, compute current FR-bound coverage from the regenerated manifest. If it's well under 80%, either ratchet the threshold from the measured baseline or sequence the WebUI/legacy backfill question explicitly.  6. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: The "unit red twice → released, campaign continues" rule doesn't account for dependents. U11 asserts concrete STOP/pass behavior for U1/U3/U4/U6/U7; if one of those is released red, U11's scenario assertions fail and U12 documents gates that don't exist.
findings.suggestion: Define release propagation: a released unit's dependents are released with it (or U12 explicitly reconciles the docs to what actually merged).  7. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: U7's structural-impact detection (routes, components, schemas, services) is language/framework-specific heuristic work hiding behind a "medium" complexity rating. False positives hard-STOP valid PRs; false negatives make `no_structural_impact` a rubber stamp. The plan gives no detail on how triggers are derived from the diff.
findings.suggestion: Specify the trigger heuristics in the unit (or narrow them to the F2 trigger list verbatim), and consider warn-first for the diff-derivation while the false-positive rate is unknown.

findings.finding: U11 tests U5’s surface gate but does not depend on U5. Its stated coverage includes U3/U7, yet its scenario has no explicit ledger or baseline-freshness failure. The DAG therefore permits an incomplete integration test to merge.
findings.suggestion: Add U5 to U11’s dependencies and add isolated U3/U7 failure assertions. Choose complexity per case: U4 targets small iterates, while U5 requires medium+. Verify each expected diagnostic so another failing gate cannot mask a missing check.

findings.finding: U9’s metric mixes “FRs/ACs” in the numerator with “live FRs” in the denominator. Also, regenerated bindings alone do not establish that a test executed and passed against the current code. This can produce misleading coverage or count stale results.
findings.suggestion: Define separate FR and AC metrics, or choose one consistent counting unit. Specify how bindings join to execution results, including commit identity, skipped tests, parameterized tests, and missing results.

findings.finding: U1 leaves the critical definition of “modified test” underspecified. Line-based detection can miss decorator or parameterization changes and mishandle renamed tests, nested suites, or multiline JS callbacks. A valid exemption code also lacks an explicit per-test scope, potentially exempting an entire diff.
findings.suggestion: Define semantic comparison using the existing test discovery/parser infrastructure, covering executable bodies and execution-affecting metadata while ignoring docstrings. Bind exemptions to individual discovered test identities and reject unresolved FRs after alias resolution.

findings.finding: U7 accepts touching `architecture.md` “and/or” an FR row, or recording `no_structural_impact`. That does not ensure the relevant artifact changed: an unrelated documentation edit could satisfy a new-route trigger, and an FR-bearing behavior change could claim no structural impact while still requiring a specification update.
findings.suggestion: Map each detected trigger to its required artifact and affected entry. Separate structural exemptions from behavioral exemptions, and reject reasons that contradict the detected change. Test unrelated artifact edits explicitly.

findings.finding: U6’s path-based exemption rule does not define runtime classification across projects. Tooling commonly lives under `scripts/` or plugin directories outside the listed exclusions; conversely, executable application code can live inside an excluded directory. This risks blocking legitimate tooling changes while allowing mislabeled runtime changes.
findings.suggestion: Reuse existing project-aware runtime classification and define handling for mixed diffs, renames, and unknown paths. Add representative monorepo and WebUI cases before enforcing the rule.

findings.finding: The plan changes record requirements across U1/U3/U8/U10 without identifying their shared schema and producer updates. U10 emits `not_run` records consumed by U3; U8 adds learning fields; exemptions require reason codes. Independent merges can temporarily make valid runs impossible if validators precede compatible writers.
findings.suggestion: Identify the existing record schema and all writers, update them alongside their validators, and add dependency edges where required. Scope enforcement to current runs or define compatibility for historical records.

findings.finding: U5 cross-checks reported commands and exit codes against an evidence index, but does not specify freshness or relevance. A passing result from an earlier revision or an unrelated suite could satisfy surface verification.
findings.suggestion: Require evidence tied to the verified revision, the detected surface, and a completed execution. Treat absent or stale evidence as failure and test both cases.  The gate-hardening direction is sound, and reuse of existing infrastructure keeps the approach proportionate. Revise the dependency graph, record compatibility, and evidence/counting contracts before implementation so the new gates enforce the intended behavior reliably.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
